content.text: Discussion at 6/1/2017 fedora tech meeting generated the solution of being explicit (in this specific code) about what is acceptable as an RDF serialization and any other mime text type being considered a binary.
Wondering – are we targeting master with this one or would this also go on the 4.7 maintenance branch?
: master for now... we will discuss on today's tech call moving almost all master commits to 4.7-maintenance.
Just an FYI - should be able to finish this up on Friday or Monday.  Had to travel this week, so that threw me off of getting this done sooner.
- I was thinking of using the strings in
POSSIBLE_RDF_RESPONSE_VARIANTS_STRING
list to determine what is a valid RDF format, and therefore a container versus binary.
However, it doesn't include
'application/n3' (contentTypeN3Alt1)

, which is (or was?) an accepted mime type.  So, when I've made my changes, tests that use 'application/n3' as the mime type now fail.  I can either change the tests, or add that content type to the POSSIBLE_RDF_RESPONSE_VARIANTS_STRING.  I'm wondering why contentTypeN3Alt1 wasn't in there in the first place and the history of POSSIBLE_RDF_RESPONSE_VARIANTS_STRING? I was trying to use that to prevent having the code have to be explicit about what it cannot accept, however, maybe being explicit is the way to go.

I realize that POSSIBLE_RDF_RESPONSE_VARIANTS_STRING list might not be the best thing to use, since it's probably for the 'Accept' header.  My goal is to make sure we don't have to have these exceptions listed everywhere ('text/plain', 'text/csv') in the code, but rather in one spot.
It looks like
POSSIBLE_RDF_RESPONSE_VARIANTS_STRING
is currently only used in integration-test code.
Using a constant for defining the allowable mime-types would be good... but I do not believe the Jersey machinery allows for an array of constants in the "@Produces" annotation.
As for the history of removing 'contentTypeN3Alt1'... that goes back a long way:
https://www.pivotaltracker.com/n/projects/684825/stories/64775424
My guess is that the underlying RDF generation machinery did not allow for "application/n3"... that may have since changed.
In looking at this more...

Jena now allows 'application/n3' for a valid RDF type, though it's not technically a mime type (yet). So, some of the tests use that mime type when _creating_ resources (versus accessing them, which would fail since the 'application/n3' is not in the @Produces list). When I limited the type checking to just that POSSIBLE_RDF_RESPONSE_VARIANTS_STRING list, the tests started failing, because Jena (used in former logic) was far more lenient.
I will change the logic I created to
not
use the POSSIBLE_RDF_RESPONSE_VARIANTS_STRING.
I would like to change the test code to use the IANA accepted mime type of 'text/n3'.  Do you have any objection to me changing that?
+1 to using 'text/n3' — much better to use the standard mime type.
: changing the tests to 'text/n3' sounds good.
resolved with:
https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo4/pull/1205
https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo4/commit/0063969d8bc04074ff5c25eae9852059ec659030
Fedora interprets "text/csv" as RDF and creates an empty container instead of a binary with the content.
See
https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo4/issues/1197
